2019_139_082019regmtg.paragraph: Troy School District's Board of Education met in regular session on August 20, 2019 at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, pairing a short action agenda with the June 2019 Treasurer's Report and unaudited year-end budget-to-actual statements for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2019. Total disbursements in the period were $7,907,454.67, comprising $4,410,270.27 in check disbursements, $3,277,659.82 in outgoing wire transfers, $213,655.24 in P-Card purchases and $14,575.34 in ACH debits, less $8,706.00 of prior-period voids. The General Fund ended the year with a fund balance of $25,406,488. Action items extended Superintendent Richard Machesky's contract through June 30, 2024.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education Regular Meeting, August 20, 2019, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, phone 248.823.4000. The agenda masthead prints 6:00 PM, while the July 16 minutes announce the August 20 regular meeting at 7:00 p.m. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Agenda**
A Red Cross District of Distinction certificate presented by Michigan American Red Cross board member Leonard Rezmierski and donor recruitment representative Kelly DeLong; consent items A-D (July 16, 2019 minutes; Treasurer's Report for May and June 2019; IA-East Schools of Choice under Section 105c for 9th grade in 2020/2021; Oakland County School Boards Association legislative priorities); personnel contract extensions; a January 2020 meeting-date change; and a closed session on attorney-client privilege.

**July 16, 2019 minutes**
Called to order at 7:00 p.m. by President Schmidt with Schmidt, Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson present, along with Superintendent Machesky, administrators DiPilato, Carrier and West, and two members of the audience. Resolution 19-072 approved consent items A-H, including the MHSAA Membership Resolution 2019/2020 and accretion of Early Childhood Educators into the Troy Education Association (Yes 7, No 0). Resolution 19-073 extended administrator contracts through June 30, 2021 without tenure (Yes 7, No 0). The Board weighed whether to repair or divest the Niles Building, with the ITT Building on Big Beaver Road raised as an alternative. Adjourned 9:15 p.m.

General Fund revenue was collected at 99.64% of the $154,394,746 budget and expenditures ran at 98.78% of the $155,576,715 budget, leaving excess revenue over expenditures of $164,016 on an opening balance of $25,242,472. Individual special revenue ending balances were $264,316 (Food Service), $0 (Troy Career Center), $557,371 (Adult and Community Education), $274 (Troy Preschool) and $283,576 (Facilities Rental). Capital projects revenue included $26,998,655 in bond proceeds and $3,867,252 of sinking fund property taxes.

**Action items**
Schools of Choice: a Section 105c resolution under the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, accepting 85 non-resident 9th grade students from outside Oakland County whose intermediate district is contiguous with Oakland ISD, for the International Academy East. Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky, rated highly effective in his fourth year, would be extended from July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2024. Rick West (Business Services), Kris Griffor (Elementary Instruction) and Jordan Harris (Employee Services) would receive successor contracts running July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2021. The January 14, 2020 Organizational and Regular Meeting would move to January 21, 2020. The closed session resolution cites the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c).

**Minutes of July 16, 2019.** Called to order at 7:00 p.m. by President Schmidt. Present: Schmidt, Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff (Secretary), Philippart and Wilson, with Superintendent Machesky, administrators DiPilato, Carrier and West, and two members of the audience. Resolution 19-072, moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Fleming, approved consent items A-H: minutes of the June 4, June 11 and June 18, 2019 meetings, workshops and closed session; the Michigan High School Athletic Association Membership Resolution 2019/2020; and accretion of Early Childhood Educators into the Troy Education Association. Vote: Yes 7, No 0. Resolution 19-073, moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Dr. Philippart, extended administrator contracts through June 30, 2021 without tenure, subject to the layoff provision in the Administrative Handbook. Named administrators included Ryan Brinks (International Academy-East), Lara Dixon (Athens High School), Remo Roncone (Troy High School), Jonathan Cross (Baker), Joe Duda (Larson), Anthony Morse (Boulan Park), Christian Mueller (Smith), elementary principals Michelle Barsh, Joyce Brasington, Brian Canfield, Mike Cottone, Erin Detmer, Tammy DiPonio, Sarah Glasser, Matt Jansen, Melanie Morey, Shari Pawlus, Jeremey Whan and Stephanie Zendler, and directors Kerry Birmingham, Jessica Carrier, Rob Carson, Tim Fulcher, Erin Keyser, Kandice Moynihan, John Pagel and Elizabeth Soggs. Vote: Yes 7, No 0. Under Other, Dr. Machesky and Mr. West discussed whether to repair or divest the Niles Building, raising renting, leasing, purchasing or constructing and mentioning the ITT Building on Big Beaver Road; Mr. Schmidt suggested a special workshop before August 20. Adjourned 9:15 p.m.; signed Gary N. Hauff, Secretary.

**Schools of Choice, Section 105c.** Michigan law requires a resolution each school year from districts intending to participate; seats were anticipated for 2020-2021 in grade 9 at the International Academy East. The resolution, exercising the option permitted by Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, would accept applications from 85 non-resident 9th grade students residing outside Oakland County whose intermediate school district is contiguous with Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries.

**OCSBA legislative priorities.** Oakland County School Boards Association resolutions covering mental health (MASB Resolutions G 9.01, G 9.05, G 9.50), local control (A 10.10, A 10.55, A 12.70), evidence-based decision making (G 11.01), unfunded mandates (A 10.20), the School Finance Research Collaborative, school aid planks A through E (A 10.25 subsections, A 10.55, A 10.05), accountability and transparency (A 6.65), lame duck parameters, universal preschool for four year olds (A 6.15 (c)) and full funding of the federal Individuals with Disabilities Education Act, which initially promised 40 percent of excess cost (A 5.01; NSBA Advocacy: IDEA). Plank E asks that the annual School Aid Budget be enacted no later than June 1 so districts can meet the June 30 budget adoption requirement. The cover letter from Birgit McQuiston, Secretary of the OCSBA Board of Directors, sets a voting window of August 1 through September 15, requires approval by at least nineteen member school districts, and reports results at the September 24 OCSBA meeting; Resolutions and Bylaws Committee members are Carol Finkelstein (248-321-7999), Marc Katz and McQuiston.

**Personnel.** Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky completed his fourth year as a highly effective superintendent and exceeded expectations in all evaluation categories, the item citing his support of oneTROY and Troy as a destination district on its journey to world class; the resolution extends his contract from July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2024 without tenure in the administrative position. Item 6.B covers Rick West (Business Services), Kris Griffor (Elementary Instruction) and Jordan Harris (Employee Services), whose contracts expire June 30, 2019; the text describes both one-year extensions and two-year successor contracts commencing July 1, 2019 and terminating June 30, 2021, without tenure.

**Meeting schedule and closed session.** The January 14, 2020 Organizational and Regular Meeting was inadvertently scheduled for the second Tuesday; the resolution moves it to January 21, 2020, consistent with third-Tuesday practice. The attached 2019 schedule lists regular meetings at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, at 7:00 p.m. on January 15, February 26, March 19, April 16, May 21, June 4 (at Athens), July 16, August 20, September 17, October 15, November 19 and December 17, and workshops at the Administrative Center, 4400 Livernois, at 6:00 p.m. on January 8, February 5, March 5 (Troy Center for Transition), April 9, May 7, June 11, September 3, October 1, November 12, December 3 and January 7, 2020. The closed session resolution, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8 (c), would take the Board into closed session to discuss an attorney-client privilege by roll call vote of trustees Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt and Wilson.
